english.title: Use snare / weapon to kill / take wild animal - England
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) used

(A)_[a self-locking snare]_
(B)_[a bow]_
(C)_[a crossbow]_
(D)_[an explosive other than ammunition for a firearm, namely **(..SPECIFY..),]_

for the purpose of killing or taking a wild animal
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 11(1)(b) and 21(1) of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.

english.notes:
(i) From the 17th October 2023, section 48 of the Agriculture (Wales) Act 2023 amends section 11 of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981. This offence applies only in England. For the offence applying in Wales and England before this date, see H4654.
(ii) See section 21(7) of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981 for place where offence deemed to have been committed for jurisdiction purposes.
(iii) See section 11(5) for presumption that animal is wild and section 27 for meaning of "wild animal".
(iv) See section 21(6) for the forfeiture provisions.

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 6 months imprisonment and / or a fine.

Where more than one animal is involved in a single offence the maximum fine shall be determined as if the person convicted had been convicted of a separate offence in respect of each animal (section 21(5)).

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex, see section 20 of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.
